prompt: Stage 2-5, level 4 with 16 gold, 96 HP, on a 2-win streak. You are 4 XP from level 5 and a 2-star 2-cost is sitting on your bench with no room on the board. What is the standard play?

options.label: Buy 4 XP for level 5 so the 2-star support joins the board for the stage 2 to 3 transition
Hold the 16 gold; you reach 5 naturally at 3-1
Roll twice for a 2-star on the caster

explanation:
Level 5 at 2-5 is the standard timing because the stage 3 opener (3-1) is the first round where boards are strong enough to take 6+ HP a loss, and a fifth unit is the single biggest jump you can buy at this point. You are 4 XP short, so it is one purchase for 4 gold, and the unit going onto the board is already a 2-star. That converts a bench unit into a win at 3-1 and a longer streak, which pays the 4 gold back in streak income within two rounds.

Waiting for the natural level at 3-1 means fighting 3-1 with four units against lobbies that already have five, and probably dropping the streak that is currently your best income source. Rolling twice for a caster upgrade at level 4 odds (55% 1-cost) is not a bad hit rate, but it spends 4 gold on a smaller improvement than the unit you already own.
principle: Standard level timings exist because the units they buy are already on your bench: level 5 at 2-5, 6 at 3-2, 7 at 4-1.
commonMistake: Sitting on 16 gold for interest at stage 2 while a 2-star rots on the bench. Interest on 16 gold is 1 gold; a fifth unit is a win.
